additional_info.subject: RE: R: ID0409303-DC/Si-D/IT-[Multiple] Iplanet - 0kW charging session CRM:01410001518
additional_info.body:
Hello Luca,
Please see the details below:
1.cri3Ps
Session was stopped from the EV side.
2.
hvDOW0
Th
e session was not initiated. Upon further analysis, we discovered that the issue was due to the cable not being connected at that time.
3.
pCX668
After reviewing the charger logs, we found that the session failed due to a problem with the isolation monitoring system, which caused the charger to enter the "EVSE_SHUTDOWN" state. This typically occurs when the isolation resistance drops below 100 kOhms, indicating a potential fault with the electrical isolation, which could pose a safety risk.
To help identify whether the issue is from our side (charger) or the vehicle side, we recommend the following steps:
Inspect Charger Cables and Connectors
: Please check the charger’s cables and connectors for any visible damage or wear that could affect the isolation monitoring system.
Check the IMD BC2
: check the IMD BC2 (Isolation Monitoring Device for Connector 2). Ensure that it's functioning properly and there are no issues with its connection or readings.
Check the Vehicle’s Charging Port
: Inspect the vehicle’s charging port for any dirt, damage, or potential issues that could cause an improper connection or short, which could affect the isolation resistance.
Additionally, after the initial failed session, a subsequent successful charging session was started with the same EV and outlet. This suggests that the issue may be intermittent or related to a specific condition at the time of the initial failure.If the problem continues or you notice any further issues with isolation, feel free to reach out, and we can assist with further troubleshooting.
We hope this helps clarify the situation, and we're happy to assist further if needed.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team - Ankita

additional_info.body:
Dear Luca Rizzi,
I apologize for the late reply. I have done the log analysis and here are my observations:
The Sicharge-D OCPP data being sent to backend is correct, attached “image1” shown is for charger
cri3Ps
, which shows the data being sent. Here we see that the Wh, W and other data is not 0. (yellow highlighted)
The same exact values are also getting received in the backend logs. See “image2”, here all the parameters are getting received correctly.( yellow highlighted)
However, we also see in the backend logs that the data is not getting parsed, hence the "0" values at the backend (red circled).
Since the data being sent is correctly getting received, this seems not an issue of Si-D but rather an issue of the OCPP backend, where the backend is not correctly parsing the data received. We request you to ask the customer to look into this issue from the backend. The values being sent by Si-D are correct.
Same is observed for
hvDOW0
as well.
With best regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: R: R: R: R: ID0409303-DC/Si-D/IT-[Multiple] Iplanet - 0kW charging session CRM:01410001518
additional_info.body:
Dear Luca Rizzi,
Sorry for the delay in reply. I have now gone through the logs again one more time.
What I have observed is that in all 3 charging sessions which you had mentioned for this case, all of them had an error which caused the charging session to not continue. So, in the logs, I could see that the charging session's RemoteStartTranscation message was seen, however, since the transactions did not technically “start” (all the sessions stopped with an error before the “charging” mode was achieved), there was no StopTranscation message sent by the charger.
Since as per the charger, the transaction did not even begin, there was no need for a StopTranscation message to be sent.
Regarding the customer's issue that these sessions are getting registered as “0kW session”, from our call with the customer, we have understood that they expect a “StopTranscation” message to appear in order to showcase the session as “stopped”. But in our case, all the sessions stopped due to an error which occurred before the actual session even began, and because of this no “StopTranscation” log was generated.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shreyas Sathe
Please do not change the subject of this Email when replying to it.
